identity: Qur'anic scripture: the complete Surat al-Adiyat (sura 100), ayat 1-11, in Uthmani rasm orthography with all diacritics and all ayah-separator marks stripped (والعديت for والعاديات, فالمغيرت for فالمغيرات, الإنسن for الإنسان, فى for في). 40 tokens, one unbroken block with zero <NL> tokens, which tells me the source rendered the sura as running text with inline ayah circles rather than one verse per line; the stripping step removed those circles exactly as it removed the Bible verse numbers in my batch-2 scripture documents. Register: rhymed oracular saj - five oath clauses (aqsam) in vv.1-5 rhyming on the tamyiz accusative, the jawab al-qasam in vv.6-8 rhyming on -ud/-id, and an eschatological rhetorical question in vv.9-11. Not prose quoting scripture: there is no framing verb, no narrator, no attribution.
law: Doctrine section M governs and outranks everything else in the file: in scripture the unit is the VERSE, because the source carries an explicit per-verse index mark, and LAW 0-prime ranks a verse index above every other typographic signal, including internal full stops. In a mushaf that mark is the ayah separator, present after every single ayah without exception - a more regular index than the Bible verse numbers section M was actually built on, not less. So: one ayah = one segment; 11 ayat = 11 segments; boundaries at 1, 3, 5, 8, 11, 15, 19, 23, 30, 34, 39. Corollaries carried over from M2: the ف- and و- that open vv.2,3,4,5,7,8,10 are not my reason for cutting (LAW 1 and LAW 2 - a connective is never a reason) and equally are not a reason to weld; the verse index simply overrides both, and it also overrides LAW 3 (parallel and coordinate items weld) and LAW 4 (a trailing subordinate clause belongs to its main clause). I explicitly override the LAW 6 table row 'scripture = 15-35 tokens': that figure is a property of Van Dyck Bible narrative, and LAW 0's central correction is that a token count is a sample statistic and never a law while the unit system is the law. These ayat run 2-7 tokens and that is simply what this source's unit is.
reasoning: STEP ZERO, unit-system identification (my open tension T9, and worth all 11 decisions here). Cues: rasm spellings (العديت, المغيرت, الإنسن, فى) that occur in no other register; saj rhyme carried across every clause; the qasam-plus-jawab frame; the closing formula إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير. This is scripture, and it is verse-indexed, so the unit is fixed before I place a single boundary. || SITE 1, indices 1, 3, 5, 8 - inside the oath chain والعديت ضبحا فالموريت قدحا فالمغيرت صبحا فأثرن به نقعا فوسطن به جمعا. This is the heaviest weld pressure in the document and the site my own LAW 3 would get wrong: five morphologically parallel oath phrases, four of them tied to the first by ف-, each closing on a tamyiz accusative - formally one coordinated oath. In prose this is the 13-name run of doc_0de3fe1bcb6c or the kobri list of doc_3484c02411e9, i.e. ONE segment. But these are vv.1-5, and section M2's precedent is exactly this shape: ف/و/ثم never separate inside a verse and never suppress a separation at a verse end. I cut all four. || SITE 2, index 11 (جمعا). End of the oath chain, pivot into the jawab al-qasam. A boundary under the verse reading (v5|v6) and the most defensible boundary under a purely syntactic reading too, so it is my safest internal cut. || SITE 3, indices 15 and 19 (لكنود, لشهيد). Both are followed by وإنه - a coordinated nominal predicate on the same subject, the textbook case for LAW 1 as revised, where doc_085c979b884f @489 welds a brand-new subject carrying its own nominal predicate. Under prose law vv.6-8 would be one segment. Under section M they are three verses. The verse index wins. If this document grades badly the loss will be concentrated here and in the oath chain, and the lesson would be that section M does not transfer from Bible to Qur'an - which I do not believe, since the ayah mark is the most regular verse index in the corpus. || SITE 4, index 23 (لشديد). Followed by أفلا يعلم, an interrogative with fresh mood and a new subject opening the eschatological section. Boundary under both readings; my highest-confidence internal cut. || SITE 5, index 30 (القبور) - the crux, and my only med. أفلا يعلم إذا بعثر ما فى القبور وحصل ما فى الصدور is ONE إذا-clause with two coordinated passive verbs sharing a single subordinator; cutting at القبور splits a subordinate clause down the middle, which LAW 3 (coordinate verbs weld) and LAW 4 (trailing subordinate clauses belong to their main clause) both forbid. The verse division nevertheless falls there: v9 ends at القبور and v10 is وحصل ما فى الصدور. This is precisely the override section M2 already logged - doc_0623277721a2 @401, where a trailing لأن DOES cut because the verse breaks there and LAW 4 is overridden. I follow the verse index, and I mark this med because it is the single cleanest test in the document of whether the verse rule really beats the syntactic rule. || SITE 6, index 34 (الصدور). End of v10, before the apodosis إن ربهم بهم يومئذ لخبير. Verse boundary and a clean syntactic joint as well; hi. || Index 39 (لخبير) is the final token, free by format. || WHERE I DO NOT CUT: nowhere the verse index does not license. Not at any of the eight ف-/و- openers for their own sake (LAW 1, LAW 2); not before إذا at 26; not inside إن الإنسن لربه لكنود; not between إن and its ism anywhere. || CALIBRATION NOTE against my batch-2 22:1 over-cutting profile: 11 boundaries over 40 tokens is 3.6 tokens per segment, far denser than any row in my LAW 6 table, so this looks like the failure mode I was told to watch. It is not the same failure. Batch 2's scripture damage came from cutting at connectives INSIDE verses; here every cut is at a verse end and every connective-only site is welded. If I am wrong here I am wrong about one thing only - extending section M across a scripture tradition - and that is a single, testable proposition rather than a relapse into the batch-1 reflex.
